name: Muttekopf
kurzbeschreibung: The Hausberg of Imst – a 2.774 m peak with climbing routes, hiking trails, and a breathtaking 360° panorama over the Lechtaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Muttekopf (2,774 m) stands as a monumental, jagged limestone summit in the southeastern Lechtal Alps, presiding majestically over the historic Tyrolean town of Imst. Characterized by severe rocky spires, vast scree basins, and expansive alpine meadows, it has drawn mountaineers and climbers for over a century. At the center of the massif lies the idyllic Muttekopf cirque, where the traditional alpine refuge Muttekopfhütte (1,934 m) welcomes weary trekkers below soaring rock towers. Reaching the summit cross yields an awe-inspiring 360-degree panorama encompassing the Zugspitze, the Wetterstein massif, the Stubai Alps, and the glaciated peaks of the Ötztal Alps.

Route & Requirements

The classic alpine ascent conveniently begins at the Alpjoch top station (2,050 m) of the Imster Bergbahnen chairlift. From Alpjoch, the panoramic Drischlsteig—a secured ledge carved into vertical limestone walls (rated T3)—descends gently to Muttekopfhütte in roughly 30 to 45 minutes. Pure hikers can also climb entirely from Hoch-Imst through the dramatic Rosengartenschlucht gorge (adding 850 vertical meters). From the refuge, the marked trail climbs steadily through the alpine pasture of Schafwanne before ascending steep, loose scree switchbacks to the Muttekopfscharte ridge saddle (2,630 m). The final summit ridge demands absolute surefootedness and a calm head for heights across rugged terrain (rated T3+/T4, UIAA grade I). Ascending from Alpjoch requires 750 vertical meters and 2.5 to 3 hours of walking (2 hours descent). Advanced vertical scramblers can tackle the celebrated Imster Klettersteig (grade C/D via ferrata). Sturdy mountaineering boots, trekking poles, alpine weather gear, and ample fluids are essential. The final rocky ridge is impassable for dogs.

Visit & Arrival

Rail travelers arrive at Imst-Pitztal mainline station via frequent ÖBB express trains. City buses run from the station forecourt into Imst center and continue to the base terminal of Imster Bergbahnen in Hoch-Imst. Motorists take the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Imst) or travel toll-free across the Fernpass highway (B179), following signs directly up to Hoch-Imst. Ample free parking is situated right beside the lift terminals. The chairlifts operate from late May through October.

Tips

Combine your descent with a thrilling ride on the Alpine Coaster Imst—the longest alpine coaster in the world—which descends from the Untermarkter Alm middle station. Stop at Muttekopfhütte to enjoy fresh handmade cheese dumplings (Kaspressknödel) and blueberry pancakes on the panoramic deck. In peak summer, start early to navigate the southern scree slopes before midday heat peaks.
